FAQs/CloudAssure/AssesmentandAdvisory.title: Assesment and Advisory
FAQs/CloudAssure/AssesmentandAdvisory.description: What are Cloud Assessment Services?Cloud Assessment and Advisory is a structured engagement that thoroughly evaluates an organization’s IT infrastructure, applications, and processes to determine cloud readiness. The outcome is a tailored roadmap for migration and modernization aligned with business objectives, operational needs, and future scalability.

FAQs/CloudAssure/CloudAssure.title: Cloud Assure
FAQs/CloudAssure/CloudAssure.description: What is Cloud Assure Service (CAS)?Cloud Assure is a comprehensive cloud management service suite designed to help enterprises manage, secure, and optimize their cloud environments across public (Yntraa Cloud, AWS, Azure), private, hybrid, and multi-cloud setups. It covers the full lifecycle from assessment and migration to operations, security, optimization, and professional services.

FAQs/CloudAssure/MigrationAssist.title: Migration Assist
FAQs/CloudAssure/MigrationAssist.description: What is Cloud Migration Assist?Cloud Migration Assist is a structured service that supports all types of migrations, including on-premises to cloud, cloud-to-cloud, and legacy environment migrations. It ensures secure and efficient movement of workloads, applications, databases, and data with minimal disruption and a controlled transition.

FAQs/CloudAssure/ProfessionalService.title: Professional Service
FAQs/CloudAssure/ProfessionalService.description: What is Cloud Professional Service?Cloud Professional Service is a specialized, project-based consulting and implementation offering under the Cloud Assure portfolio. It helps organizations maximize cloud adoption, transformation, and innovation through tailored engagements spanning the entire cloud lifecycle—from strategy and adoption to optimization and continuous improvement.

FAQs/ManagedSolutions/ManagedDatabases.title: Managed Databases
FAQs/ManagedSolutions/ManagedDatabases.description: What is Yntraa Cloud Managed Database as a Service (MDBaaS)?Yntraa Cloud MDBaaS is a fully managed database solution that offers enterprises scalable, secure, and high-performance databases without the need to manage the underlying infrastructure.

FAQs/ManagedSolutions/ResiliencyAssuranc.title: Resiliency Assurance Service
FAQs/ManagedSolutions/ResiliencyAssuranc.description: What is a Disaster?Disaster is a natural or man-made (or technological) hazard resulting in an event of substantial extent causing significant physical damage or destruction or loss.

FAQs/Other Services/File Storage.title: File Storage
FAQs/Other Services/File Storage.description: What is File Storage in STaaS?File Storage offers shared access using standard file protocols (NFS/SMB), suitable for collaborative workspaces, media editing, and centralized storage environments.

FAQs/Storage/ObjectStorage.title: Object Storage
FAQs/Storage/ObjectStorage.description: What is object storage in the context of Yntraa Cloud?Object storage is a scalable and durable storage solution for managing unstructured data such as files, images, videos, and backups.

Knowledgebase/DifferenceBetweenL2Network.title: Difference Between L2 Networks and VPC
Knowledgebase/DifferenceBetweenL2Network.description: An L2 network provides connectivity at the data link layer, allowing devices within the same network segment to communicate directly, while a Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) creates an isolated virtual network environment in the cloud. These components work together to support secure and flexible network design.

Knowledgebase/IPv4Networking.title: What is IPv4 Networking?
Knowledgebase/IPv4Networking.description: Internet Protocol version 4(IPv4) is the fourth generation of the Internet Protocol, and it remains the most commonly used system for assigning addresses to devices connected to a network. An IPv4 address is made up of four numbers separated by dots—like 10.0.1.15—and each address is unique, ensuring that data sent over the internet reaches the right device.

Knowledgebase/WhatisaVirtualFirewallinth.title: What is a Virtual Firewall in the Cloud?
Knowledgebase/WhatisaVirtualFirewallinth.description: A virtual firewall is a software-based tool used to protect cloud systems. Just like a physical firewall protects a building from fire, a virtual firewall helps protect your cloud network from harmful or unwanted traffic. It controls the flow of data between different parts of your system and blocks anything suspicious or risky. This keeps your applications and data safe, whether traffic is coming from outside the cloud or moving between parts of the same system.

Knowledgebase/WhatisaVPC.title: What is a VPC?
Knowledgebase/WhatisaVPC.description: A Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) is a secure, isolated section of a public cloud where you can deploy and manage your cloud resources—such as instances, databases, and applications—with full control over networking and security. With a VPC, you define your own IP address ranges, create subnets, configure routing tables, and set up firewalls and gateways, allowing you to build a custom network architecture tailored to your needs.

Knowledgebase/WhatisInstances.title: What is Instances?
Knowledgebase/WhatisInstances.description: Cloud computing allows users to run virtual machines called instances, which are flexible, on-demand servers that can run different operating systems. The two most common types of instances available in cloud environments are Linux instances and Windows instances. Both serve unique purposes and cater to different application needs.

Knowledgebase/WhatisIPAddressSubnetTiera.title: What is IP Address, Subnet, Tier and CIDR?
Knowledgebase/WhatisIPAddressSubnetTiera.description: Every device or service in a network—whether it's a virtual machine, load balancer, or database—needs a unique IP address to talk to other devices. It’s like a digital address for communication. For example, a instance may be assigned 192.168.1.10, which allows it to send and receive data across the network.

Knowledgebase/WorkingwithVPNConnectionsi.title: Working with VPN Connections in a VPC
Knowledgebase/WorkingwithVPNConnectionsi.description: The VPC feature on Yntraa Cloud provides advanced networking capabilities for use with virtual private networks (VPN) gateways and connections over an IPSec tunnel. Yntraa Cloud gives the ability to create VPN to access virtual machines inside a VPC.

ReleaseNotes/Ver1000.title: Version 1.0.0.0
ReleaseNotes/Ver1000.description: We are excited to announce the general availability of Yntraa Cloud Platform, a modern cloud infrastructure platform designed to support enterprise applications, data platforms, and digital services.

Subscribers/AccountCentre/AccountProfile.title: Account Profile
Subscribers/AccountCentre/AccountProfile.description: The profile section provides a centralized view of your account information and primary contact details. It enables you to view and manage essential account information, including organization details, contact information, email address, and mobile number. This page also displays the account verification status, helping ensure that your account information remains accurate and up to date.

Subscribers/AccountCentre/ServiceBalance.title: Service Balance
Subscribers/AccountCentre/ServiceBalance.description: The service balance provides a consolidated view of your available wallet balance, credit voucher balance, and transaction history. It enables you to monitor the funds available for service consumption, manage your wallet, apply credit vouchers, and review wallet and voucher transactions. You can also search, filter, and download transaction records, helping you efficiently track and manage your service balance and payment activities.

Subscribers/AccountCentre/Subscriptionsa.title: Subscriptions and Services
Subscribers/AccountCentre/Subscriptionsa.description: A subscription is a record created whenever a new resource is purchased or a service is activated. In other words, a subscription is a financial ‘agreement’ that links the item that has been purchased, its value, and its renewal frequency.

Subscribers/AccountCentre/ViewingService.title: Viewing Service Usage
Subscribers/AccountCentre/ViewingService.description: The usage feed provides a consolidated view of usage records for your subscribed services. It enables you to monitor subscription usage by displaying key details such as subscription information, usage period, and related charge information. You can also search, filter, and download the usage records to help review and track service consumption during the selected period.

Subscribers/AccountCentre/ViewingSubscri.title: Viewing Subscription Charges
Subscribers/AccountCentre/ViewingSubscri.description: The unbilled charges provides a consolidated view of charges that have been incurred for your active subscriptions but have not yet been included in an invoice. It enables you to monitor the estimated charges accumulated during the current billing cycle, helping you track your spending before the invoice is generated. The page includes charges for both fixed subscriptions and usage-based services, ensuring better visibility into ongoing costs.

Subscribers/AddingTeamMembers.title: Adding Team Members
Subscribers/AddingTeamMembers.description: One Yotta is Yotta’s unified customer portal that provides a single, secure platform to manage your account, services, assets, billing, and infrastructure monitoring. It centralizes essential management tasks, giving you complete visibility into your environment and enabling you to efficiently manage single or multiple deployments through an intuitive dashboard.

Subscribers/Compute/Autoscale/CreatingAu.title: Creating Autoscale Groups
Subscribers/Compute/Autoscale/CreatingAu.description: Creating an autoscale group enables automatic scaling of compute instances based on workload demand and defined scaling policies. This helps maintain application performance, improve availability, and optimize resource utilization by automatically adding or removing instances as needed.

Subscribers/Compute/Autoscale/Modifying.title: Modifying Configurations
Subscribers/Compute/Autoscale/Modifying.description: The modifying configurations allows you to update the settings of an existing autoscale group. You can disable the group, access its configuration settings, update the required parameters, and apply the changes. The available configurations include compute resources, OS image, and disk settings. After reviewing the updates, you can confirm the changes to save and apply the new configuration.

Subscribers/Compute/Autoscale/ViewingAut.title: Viewing Autoscale Groups
Subscribers/Compute/Autoscale/ViewingAut.description: This section provides an overview of all configured autoscaling groups in your environment. You can view the available groups, monitor their status, and access details to manage or review their configurations. This view helps you track and manage the resources associated with autoscaling.

Subscribers/Compute/ManagedKubernetes/Ac.title: Accessing a Cluster using the Command Line
Subscribers/Compute/ManagedKubernetes/Ac.description: You can access and control the Kubernetes clusters from the command line using the kubeconfig manifest for the cluster. Each cluster has a unique manifest which is required to identify and target the cluster using the kubectl utility.

Subscribers/Compute/ManagedKubernetes/Ac.title: Accessing the Kubernetes Dashboard
Subscribers/Compute/ManagedKubernetes/Ac.description: To access the dashboard in Kubernetes version 1.24 and onwards, follow these steps:

Subscribers/Compute/ManagedKubernetes/Ba.title: Backuping and Restoring ETCD
Subscribers/Compute/ManagedKubernetes/Ba.description: This section describes the procedure for backing up and restoring the Kubernetes ETCD database. It covers creating ETCD snapshots, verifying snapshot integrity, and restoring ETCD in the event of cluster corruption, accidental data deletion, control plane failures, or disaster recovery scenarios.

Subscribers/Compute/ManagedKubernetes/Cr.title: Creating a Kubernetes Cluster
Subscribers/Compute/ManagedKubernetes/Cr.description: A Kubernetes cluster is a managed environment for deploying and managing containerized applications. Creating a Kubernetes cluster enables you to automate application deployment, scaling, and management while ensuring high availability, efficient resource utilization, and simplified operations across your cloud environment.

Subscribers/Compute/ManagedKubernetes/In.title: Installing ACS CSI Driver on K8s Cluster
Subscribers/Compute/ManagedKubernetes/In.description: This section describes the process for installing and configuring the Apache CloudStack (ACS) Container Storage Interface (CSI) driver on a Kubernetes cluster using Helm.

Subscribers/Compute/ManagedKubernetes/In.title: Installing Prometheus and Grafana
Subscribers/Compute/ManagedKubernetes/In.description: This section describes the process for deploying Prometheus and Grafana on a Kubernetes cluster using the kube-prometheus-stack Helm chart from the Prometheus Community repository.

Subscribers/Compute/ManagedKubernetes/Ku.title: Kubernetes Dashboard
Subscribers/Compute/ManagedKubernetes/Ku.description: The Kubernetes Dashboard is a web-based user interface that provides a visual representation of a cluster's resources and enables easier management and monitoring. Here's an overview of the dashboard:

Subscribers/Compute/ManagedKubernetes/Ma.title: Managing Kubernetes Cluster Operations
Subscribers/Compute/ManagedKubernetes/Ma.description: Manage Kubernetes cluster operations to control the lifecycle and capacity of your cluster. These operations enable you to stop the cluster for maintenance, scale resources to meet workload demands, and delete the cluster when it is no longer required, helping you efficiently manage your Kubernetes environment.

Subscribers/Compute/ManagedKubernetes/Ma.title: Managing Networks Rules
Subscribers/Compute/ManagedKubernetes/Ma.description: Managing Network Rules enables you to control and regulate network traffic for Kubernetes workloads by configuring essential networking rules. It provides options to define firewall rules for traffic filtering, create port forwarding rules for secure access to applications, and configure load balancing rules to distribute incoming traffic across multiple resources.

Subscribers/Compute/ManagedKubernetes/Sc.title: Scaling Kubernetes Clusters
Subscribers/Compute/ManagedKubernetes/Sc.description: Scaling a Kubernetes cluster allows you to adjust its compute capacity by increasing or decreasing the number of worker nodes based on workload demands. This helps maintain application performance, optimize resource utilization, and ensure high availability while efficiently managing infrastructure costs.

Subscribers/Compute/ManagedKubernetes/Vi.title: Viewing Kubernetes Cluster Details
Subscribers/Compute/ManagedKubernetes/Vi.description: View the kubernetes cluster details to access comprehensive information about the cluster, including its configuration, node information, networking, and current status. Reviewing these details helps you monitor cluster health, verify settings, and troubleshoot issues effectively.

Subscribers/Compute/ManagedKubernetes/Vi.title: Viewing Kubernetes Clusters
Subscribers/Compute/ManagedKubernetes/Vi.description: View kubernetes clusters and access essential details such as cluster name, public IP address, autoscaling configuration, and creation date. Monitor cluster information from a centralized view to quickly review configurations and manage your Kubernetes environments efficiently.

Subscribers/Compute/OtherLinuxInstances/.title: Connecting to a Linux Instance
Subscribers/Compute/OtherLinuxInstances/.description: After creating a linux instance, you can connect to it remotely to perform administrative tasks, install software, configure applications, and manage system resources. Secure Shell (SSH) is the standard method used to establish a secure connection to a linux instance. Depending on your operating system, you can connect to the instance using different tools and methods.

Subscribers/Compute/OtherLinuxInstances/.title: Creating Linux Instances
Subscribers/Compute/OtherLinuxInstances/.description: Create a  linux instance to deploy a instance for running  linux-based applications and workloads in the cloud. During creation, you configure the required compute, storage, networking, and other settings to provision an instance that meets your workload requirements.

Subscribers/Compute/OtherLinuxInstances/.title: Managing Alerts
Subscribers/Compute/OtherLinuxInstances/.description: Alerts help you monitor the health and performance of your linux instance by notifying you when predefined conditions are met. You can create, view, modify, or delete alerts and manage email recipients to ensure the appropriate users receive notifications. Managing alerts enables you to proactively monitor your linux instance and respond promptly to important events.

Subscribers/Compute/OtherLinuxInstances/.title: Managing Instance Restore Points
Subscribers/Compute/OtherLinuxInstances/.description: Instance restore points help protect your linux instances by creating point-in-time recovery snapshots. You can create restore points before performing maintenance, configuration changes, or updates, and restore the instance to a previous state if required. You can also delete restore points that are no longer needed to optimize resource usage. This section explains how to create, restore, and delete instance restore points for a linux instance.

Subscribers/Compute/OtherLinuxInstances/.title: Managing Linux Instance Operations
Subscribers/Compute/OtherLinuxInstances/.description: You can manage the lifecycle of linux instance by restarting, force stopping, renaming, or deleting. These operations help you maintain service availability, resolve operational issues, organize resources, and manage your cloud infrastructure efficiently.

Subscribers/Compute/OtherLinuxInstances/.title: Managing Networks
Subscribers/Compute/OtherLinuxInstances/.description: Manage the networking configuration of your linux instance to control connectivity and communication with other resources. You can configure network settings, and manage network access to ensure secure and reliable communication for your workloads.

Subscribers/Compute/OtherLinuxInstances/.title: Managing Volume
Subscribers/Compute/OtherLinuxInstances/.description: Manage volumes to monitor and protect the storage resources attached to your instances. Volume management allows you to view attached disks, create disk restore points to safeguard data before changes, and create custom images for rapid instance deployment and recovery. These operations help ensure data protection, simplify backup and restoration, and maintain consistent storage configurations across your cloud environment.

Subscribers/Compute/OtherLinuxInstances/.title: Reconfiguring Linux Instances
Subscribers/Compute/OtherLinuxInstances/.description: Reconfigure a linux instance to change its compute and root disk configuration when your workload requirements change. Updating the compute pack and root disk allows you to allocate resources that better match your application's performance and capacity needs.

Subscribers/Compute/OtherLinuxInstances/.title: Viewing Details of Linux Instances
Subscribers/Compute/OtherLinuxInstances/.description: View detailed information about a linux instance, including its configuration, status, networking, storage, and resource allocation. Reviewing these details helps you monitor the instance and verify its settings for effective management.

Subscribers/Compute/OtherLinuxInstances/.title: Viewing Graphs
Subscribers/Compute/OtherLinuxInstances/.description: Graphs provide a visual representation of the performance and resource utilization of your linux instance. You can monitor key metrics such as CPU, memory, network traffic, and disk activity over time to track usage patterns, identify performance trends, and help ensure the instance operates efficiently.

Subscribers/Compute/OtherLinuxInstances/.title: Viewing Linux Instances
Subscribers/Compute/OtherLinuxInstances/.description: The linux instances page lets you view and monitor all linux instances in your cloud environment. It displays key instance details and status information, helping you quickly identify, access, and manage your linux-based workloads.

Subscribers/Compute/OtherLinuxInstances/.title: Viewing Utilisation
Subscribers/Compute/OtherLinuxInstances/.description: Utilisation reports provide historical usage details for your linux instance. You can view daily maximum, minimum, and average readings across all supported parameters. The utilisation table presents this information in a clear date‑wise format, and you can download the report as a .csv file for further analysis.

Subscribers/Compute/RHELInstances/Connec.title: Connecting to a RHEL Instance
Subscribers/Compute/RHELInstances/Connec.description: Connecting to a RHEL instance allows you to securely access and manage your virtual machine remotely. You can connect using either a password or an SSH key pair. SSH key-based authentication is recommended as it provides a more secure way to access your instance.

Subscribers/Compute/RHELInstances/Creati.title: Creating RHEL Instances

Subscribers/GettingStartedonYntraaCloud.title: Getting Started
Subscribers/GettingStartedonYntraaCloud.description: This section guides you through the basic steps to create and launch your first workload on the Yntraa Cloud portal. You will learn how to set up the required networking components, choose the right compute resources, configure storage and access settings, apply security rules, and finally create a customer workload instance.

Subscribers/intro.title: Introduction
Subscribers/intro.description: Yntraa Cloud is a powerful, all-in-one solution designed to make managing your cloud and network services simple and efficient. Whether you are a business, an organization, or an individual, Yntraa Cloud provides everything you need to keep your digital infrastructure running smoothly.

Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/L2 Networ.title: Adding an L2 Network
Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/L2 Networ.description: Adding an L2 network allows you to create a network layer that enables connectivity within the same broadcast domain. It is useful for setting up isolated or internal networks, supporting seamless communication between resources within a defined environment.

Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/L2 Networ.title: Managing L2 Networks Operations
Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/L2 Networ.description: Managing an L2 network allows you to maintain its availability and lifecycle. Manage an L2 network to perform actions such as restarting the network to restore connectivity and deleting unused networks to free resources and keep your network environment organised.

Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/L2 Networ.title: Viewing L2 Networks
Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/L2 Networ.description: The viewing L2 networks section provides you a centralized view of all Layer 2 (L2) networks within the cloud environment. This page helps you to monitor, identify, and manage configured L2 networks associated with different workloads and availability zones.

Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/LoadBalan.title: Accessing the Alteon LBI Control Panel
Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/LoadBalan.description: The Alteon Load Balancer Instance (LBI) control panel is a web-based management interface that enables you to configure, monitor, and manage your Alteon LBI. Accessing the control panel allows you to perform advanced load balancing, traffic management, application delivery, and security configurations to ensure high availability, performance, and reliability for your applications.

Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/LoadBalan.title: Creating a Load Balancer Instance
Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/LoadBalan.description: Creating a load balancer instance provisions a dedicated load balancing appliance within your virtual network to distribute application traffic across multiple backend resources. Create a load balancer instance to improve application availability, optimize traffic distribution, and enhance performance by directing client requests to healthy backend servers.

Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/LoadBalan.title: Managing Instance Restore Point
Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/LoadBalan.description: Instance restore points help protect your load balancer instances by creating point-in-time recovery snapshots. You can create restore points before performing maintenance, configuration changes, or updates, and restore the instance to a previous state if required. You can also delete restore points that are no longer needed to optimize resource usage. This section explains how to create, restore, and delete instance restore points for a load balancer instance.

Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/LoadBalan.title: Managing Load Balance Instance Operations
Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/LoadBalan.description: You can manage the lifecycle of load balancer by restarting, force stopping, renaming, or deleting. These operations help you maintain service availability, resolve operational issues, organize resources, and manage your cloud infrastructure efficiently.

Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/LoadBalan.title: Managing Networks
Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/LoadBalan.description: Managing Networks allows you to configure the network connectivity of a Load Balancer instance by adding network interfaces and assigning secondary IP addresses. These capabilities help improve connectivity, support multiple network requirements, and enable more flexible traffic management within the VPC.

Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/LoadBalan.title: Reconfiguring Load Balancer Instance
Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/LoadBalan.description: Reconfigure a load balancer instance to change its compute configuration when your workload requirements change. Updating the compute pack allows you to allocate resources that better match your application's performance and capacity needs.

Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/LoadBalan.title: Viewing Load Balancer Instance Details
Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/LoadBalan.description: Load balancer instance details provide an overview of the instance, including its current status, configuration, internal information, and network details. This information helps you monitor the instance, verify its configuration, and manage network connectivity effectively.

Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/NATGatewa.title: Managing IP Addresses
Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/NATGatewa.description: Each virtual gateway comes with a default IPv4 address that belongs to the Virtual Gateway governing the network. The default (source - NAT) IPv4 address can be used to access the Virtual Gateway publicly or via Remote Access (RA) VPN.

Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/NATGatewa.title: Managing NAT Gateway Operations
Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/NATGatewa.description: NAT Gateway operations allow you to manage the lifecycle and availability of a NAT Gateway within a Virtual Private Cloud (VPC). These operations include restarting the NAT Gateway to restore or refresh its service availability and deleting the NAT Gateway when it is no longer required. Before deletion, ensure that all associated configurations, such as firewall associations and IP address assignments, are removed.

Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/NATGatewa.title: Viewing NAT Gateway Instances
Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/NATGatewa.description: A NAT Gateway enables private instances in a virtual network to access the internet without assigning them public IP addresses. Viewing a NAT Gateway instance helps you verify its configuration and status, ensuring secure and reliable outbound internet connectivity.

Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/NATGatewa.title: Viewing NAT Gateway Overview
Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/NATGatewa.description: The NAT gateway overview helps you view the current configuration and operational status of the gateway. Reviewing the overview enables you to validate the gateway's settings, monitor its performance, and manage it more effectively.

Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/NATGatewa.title: Viewing NAT Gateways
Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/NATGatewa.description: The viewing NAT Gateways section provides an overview of all created NAT Gateways within the system. You can view the list of NAT Gateways along with their relevant details, enabling easy monitoring and management of configured network connectivity resources.

Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/VirtualFi.title: Creating a Virtual Firewall
Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/VirtualFi.description: Creating a virtual firewall allows you to deploy a firewall instance to secure and manage network traffic for your cloud resources. It helps protect your environment by applying the required security configuration and traffic control policies during deployment.

Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/VirtualFi.title: Managing Alerts
Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/VirtualFi.description: Alerts help you monitor the health and performance of your virtual firewall by notifying you when predefined conditions are met. You can create, view, modify, or delete alerts and manage email recipients to ensure the appropriate users receive notifications. Managing alerts enables you to proactively monitor your virtual firewall and respond promptly to important events.

Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/VirtualFi.title: Managing Firewall Instance Operations
Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/VirtualFi.description: Managing virtual firewall operations allows you to perform essential administrative tasks on your Virtual Firewall, such as restarting, force stopping, renaming, and deleting it. These operations help you maintain the firewall, manage its lifecycle, and ensure efficient administration of your cloud resources.

Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/VirtualFi.title: Managing Instance Restore Points
Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/VirtualFi.description: Instance Restore Points help protect your instances by creating recovery points that can be used to restore them to a previous state when needed. Managing restore points allows you to create new recovery points, restore an instance from an existing restore point, and delete restore points that are no longer required. This helps ensure reliable data protection, simplifies recovery, and enables efficient management of instance backups.

Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/VirtualFi.title: Managing Volume
Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/VirtualFi.description: Manage volumes to monitor and protect the storage resources attached to your instances. Volume management allows you to view attached disks, create disk restore points to safeguard data before changes, and create custom images for rapid instance deployment and recovery. These operations help ensure data protection, simplify backup and restoration, and maintain consistent storage configurations across your cloud environment.

Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/VirtualFi.title: Networking Management
Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/VirtualFi.description: Networking management keeps your virtual firewall instance connected securely and ensures smooth traffic flow. It involves expanding connectivity when needed, assigning extra addresses for flexibility, and removing unused interfaces to keep configurations clean.

Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/VirtualFi.title: Reconfiguring Virtual Firewall
Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/VirtualFi.description: Reconfigure a virtual firewall to replace its current firewall appliance with a different one that better meets your operational and security requirements. This operation updates the firewall configuration by applying the selected appliance.

Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/VirtualFi.title: Viewing Graphs
Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/VirtualFi.description: Graphs display key performance metrics of your Virtual Firewall instance. You can view CPU, RAM, network traffic, and disk activity on a 24‑hour time scale with a 30‑day trend line. Graphs help you track utilization patterns and configure custom alerts to manage performance effectively.

Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/VirtualFi.title: Viewing Utilisation
Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/VirtualFi.description: Utilisation reports provide historical usage details for your Virtual Firewall instance. You can view daily maximum, minimum, and average readings across all supported parameters. The utilisation table presents this information in a clear date‑wise format, and you can download the report as a .csv file for further analysis.

Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/VirtualFi.title: Viewing Virtual Firewall Instance Details
Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/VirtualFi.description: Firewall instance details give a simple overview of the system. They show its current status, basic identifiers, and network connections. This information is important because it helps you track resources, manage connectivity, and keep communication secure.

Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/VirtualFi.title: Viewing Virtual Firewalls
Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/VirtualFi.description: The virtual firewalls list provides you a centralized view of all configured virtual firewall appliances within the cloud environment. Virtual Firewalls are software-defined firewall appliances that help protect cloud instances and networks by controlling and securing network traffic.

Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/VirtualPr.title: Creating a VPC
Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/VirtualPr.description: A Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) is a private virtual network that provides a secure environment for your cloud resources. It helps you organize and manage your network while controlling communication between resources.

Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/VirtualPr.title: Creating Subnets and Tiers
Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/VirtualPr.description: A VPC subnet is a smaller, segmented network within a VPC that helps organise and isolate cloud resources, while tiers define how these subnets are structured for different application layers.

Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/VirtualPr.title: Managing Access Control List
Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/VirtualPr.description: Access Control Lists (ACLs) in a Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) help control and manage network traffic by defining access rules for resources. ACL management includes creating ACLs, updating their names, adding or modifying rules, applying ACLs to network tiers, and removing ACLs when they are no longer required. These operations help maintain effective network access control and security policies within the VPC.

Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/VirtualPr.title: Managing VPC Instances
Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/VirtualPr.description: VPC instances represent the virtual machines running within your Virtual Private Cloud. This section helps you monitor their status and perform basic operations to keep your cloud resources running efficiently and reliably.

Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/VirtualPr.title: Reconfiguring a VPC
Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/VirtualPr.description: The reconfigure section shows your current VPC subscription details and lets you update the networking pack based on changing requirements. It helps you adjust your network setup to better match your workload needs and keep your cloud environment optimized and up to date.

Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/VirtualPr.title: Viewing VPC Details
Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/VirtualPr.description: This section provides an overview of important information about your VPC, helping you understand and manage it easily from a single place.

Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/VirtualPr.title: ViewingVPCs
Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/VirtualPr.description: Viewing available VPCs provides a list of all configured virtual private clouds and select the appropriate VPC for your networking requirements.

Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/VirtualPr.title: VPC Operations
Subscribers/NetworkandSecurity/VirtualPr.description: This section help you manage your VPC efficiently after it is created. You can perform key actions to monitor, update, and maintain your VPC, ensuring it continues to support your workload and network requirements effectively.

Subscribers/Other Services/ServicesOffer.title: Services Offered
Subscribers/Other Services/ServicesOffer.description: The following table provides a list of additional services along with their respective categories and service types. These offerings are designed to support a variety of business, infrastructure, and operational requirements.

Subscribers/Other Services/Subscribingto.title: Subscribing to a Service
Subscribers/Other Services/Subscribingto.description: By subscribing to a service, you can utilize additional cloud services designed to meet your infrastructure and operational needs. The platform enables seamless service management from a single location.

Subscribers/SigningIn.title: Signing In
Subscribers/SigningIn.description: The Yntraa Cloud portal is a secure web-based interface for accessing and managing your cloud resources. Sign in to authenticate your account and access the features and services available.

Subscribers/SigningUp.title: Signing Up
Subscribers/SigningUp.description: The cloud portal provides a secure web-based interface for managing your cloud resources. Sign up to create an account and gain access to the portal's features and services.

Subscribers/Storage/BlockVolumes/Creatin.title: Creating Data Disk
Subscribers/Storage/BlockVolumes/Creatin.description: A data disk is additional storage attached to a cloud instance for storing application data, files, databases, and other workloads separately from the system disk. Creating a data disk in Yntraa Cloud helps improve data management, provides flexibility to scale storage as needed, and ensures better performance and organization of your cloud resources.

Subscribers/Storage/BlockVolumes/Creatin.title: Creating Disk Restore Points and Volume
Subscribers/Storage/BlockVolumes/Creatin.description: Disk restore points capture the state of a block volume at a specific point in time, allowing you to restore the source volume or create a new volume from the captured data. This enables reliable backup, recovery, and rapid provisioning of additional volumes while helping protect data and maintain business continuity.

Subscribers/Storage/BlockVolumes/Creatin.title: Creating Restore Point Schedules
Subscribers/Storage/BlockVolumes/Creatin.description: You can create restore point policies for your root and data disks. These schedules enable for strategic management of data retention policies and can be used as an alternative backup solution.

Subscribers/Storage/BlockVolumes/Managin.title: Managing Operations
Subscribers/Storage/BlockVolumes/Managin.description: Managing block volume operation enables you to control the lifecycle and availability of storage volumes throughout your environment. You can perform essential volume management tasks, such as attaching or detaching volumes from instances, downloading volume data when needed, and removing volumes that are no longer required. These operations help maintain storage efficiency, support changing workload requirements, and ensure that storage resources remain organized and available.

Subscribers/Storage/BlockVolumes/Resizin.title: Resizing the Block Volume
Subscribers/Storage/BlockVolumes/Resizin.description: Resizing a block volume enables you to modify its storage capacity and configuration as needed. It allows you to adjust disk size and select the appropriate tier, helping ensure efficient and flexible storage management.

Subscribers/Storage/BlockVolumes/Viewing.title: Viewing Block Volume Details
Subscribers/Storage/BlockVolumes/Viewing.description: Viewing block volume details allows you to monitor and manage the additional storage attached to your cloud instances. In Yntraa Cloud, you can view key details such as volume name, attached instance, and storage utilization to track disk usage, optimize resource management, and maintain better control over your cloud infrastructure.

Subscribers/Storage/BlockVolumes/Viewing.title: Viewing Block Volumes
Subscribers/Storage/BlockVolumes/Viewing.description: Viewing block volumes allows you to monitor and manage the additional storage attached to your cloud instances. In Yntraa Cloud, you can view key details such as volume name, attached instance, and storage utilization to track disk usage, optimize resource management, and maintain better control over your cloud infrastructure.

Subscribers/Storage/ObjectStorageBuckets.title: Adding Object in Bucket
Subscribers/Storage/ObjectStorageBuckets.description: Adding an object enables you to upload and store data within an object storage bucket. It allows you to efficiently manage files and unstructured data while ensuring they are securely stored and easily accessible when required.

Subscribers/Storage/ObjectStorageBuckets.title: Creating Object Storage
Subscribers/Storage/ObjectStorageBuckets.description: Creating object storage enables you to set up a scalable and reliable storage environment for storing and managing various types of data. It allows you to efficiently organize, access, and manage data while providing flexibility, security, and optimized storage capabilities.

Subscribers/Storage/ObjectStorageBuckets.title: Deleting Object Bucket
Subscribers/Storage/ObjectStorageBuckets.description: The delete object storage bucket feature allows you to permanently remove an object storage bucket that is no longer required.

Subscribers/Storage/ObjectStorageBuckets.title: Feature List and Integration Details
Subscribers/Storage/ObjectStorageBuckets.description: The feature list and integration details section provides an overview of the core capabilities and integration aspects of the Object Storage service. It outlines the standard and service-specific integration touchpoints that enable seamless provisioning, management, and monitoring of storage resources.

Subscribers/Storage/ObjectStorageBuckets.title: Viewing Object Storage Bucket
Subscribers/Storage/ObjectStorageBuckets.description: Viewing object storage bucket shows all the object storage buckets in your cloud environment. Each bucket is listed with key information, including the cluster name, number of objects, storage Size, and creation time, allowing you to quickly review its status and usage.

Subscribers/Storage/ObjectStorageBuckets.title: Viewing Object Storage Bucket Details
Subscribers/Storage/ObjectStorageBuckets.description: Viewing object storage bucket details allows you to review the bucket configuration, availability status, storage usage, and activity metrics. It helps you monitor bucket performance, track data utilization, and access important information required for effective storage management.

Subscribers/SystemRequirements.title: System Requirements
Subscribers/SystemRequirements.description: To ensure optimal performance and full functionality of the Yntraa Cloud, your system must meet the following requirements:

Subscribers/ToolsandUtilities/AddingVPNG.title: Adding VPN Gateways
Subscribers/ToolsandUtilities/AddingVPNG.description: VPN Gateways allow you to establish secure connections between networks and cloud resources. The Yntraa Cloud Console enables you to create and manage VPN Gateways to ensure safe and reliable communication using encrypted tunnels over the internet.

Subscribers/ToolsandUtilities/ManagingCu.title: Managing Custom Templates and Images
Subscribers/ToolsandUtilities/ManagingCu.description: Custom templates and images help standardize and simplify the deployment of cloud resources. You can create custom images from existing instances for future reuse and delete custom images that are no longer required. Managing custom templates and images enables consistent deployments while keeping your image repository organized and up to date.

Subscribers/ToolsandUtilities/ManagingIn.title: Managing Instance and Disk Restore Points
Subscribers/ToolsandUtilities/ManagingIn.description: Instance and disk restore points provide a reliable way to recover workloads and storage resources when required. You can restore an instance to a previous state, create a new volume or image from a disk restore point, and delete disk restore points that are no longer needed. Managing restore points helps ensure data protection, simplifies recovery operations, and optimizes storage management.

Subscribers/ToolsandUtilities/ManagingSS.title: Managing SSH Public Key Pair
Subscribers/ToolsandUtilities/ManagingSS.description: SSH public key pairs enable secure, password-free authentication for accessing cloud instances. You can generate a new SSH key pair, upload an existing public key, or delete a public key that is no longer needed. Managing SSH public key pairs helps maintain secure access while ensuring that only authorized keys are available for instance authentication.
